svg.title: TOPAK H1 — The corpus: layers, precedence, and how a change moves through them
svg.desc: TOPAK is a design corpus in its genesis phase. The checkpoint is the state of record and wins over the narrative; records are immutable after ratification except by typed History rows; the narrative and the glossary are cut with each checkpoint; derived analyses are dated and frozen; specifications, the floor, the reference and the rehearsal are evidence; manifests measure every cut at the commit it measured, and the reference pins what it follows.

text.tspan: The corpus: layers, precedence, and how a change moves through them

g.text: TOPAK is a design corpus in its genesis phase. The checkpoint is the state of record and wins over the narrative; records are immutable after ratification except by typed History rows; the narrative and the glossary are cut with each checkpoint; derived analyses are dated and frozen; specifications, the floor, the reference and the rehearsal are evidence; manifests measure every cut at the commit it measured, and the reference pins

text.tspan: 1 · Precedence: who wins, who explains, who is evidence, who measures

svg.text: Current: Genesis Checkpoint G12 (2026.11.16, tag G12). Each checkpoint is one cut, never revised: what each record says, what was ratified and by whom, what is owed, what is open, and the manifest that measures it. G12 is the first at which the prover's two known unsound cases are reported upstream, and the first with ten more proof modules, every one under a Proposed record (G12 header).

Where the narrative and the checkpoint disagree, the checkpoint wins. G12 names ToO revision 15 as standing, not revised at G12, and behind it on both batches, the upstream report and its fixes, the proofs of Workflow and Mesh, and twenty-two Proposed records (items 14, 109); revision 16 is cut against G12 afterwards. Batch 40 (2026.11.17, ADR-0033 A19 and A20) comes after the cut.
checkpoints/README.md names G12 and holds the 2026.09.30 layout map, the one place stale paths resolve.
ADR-0001 onward, one file each, numbered in the order settled; 76 files to ADR-0077, ADR-0014 reserved; twenty-two added since G11, all Proposed
(G12 §1.1). Sixteen amendments pending at G12, fifteen on a Proposed record and ADR-0033 A19 alone (R14); A19 ratified in Batch 40, so fifteen
are pending, every one on a Proposed record (ADR-0033 Pending line).
Never edited after ratification except by a typed History row: an amendment, an erratum, a revision before ratification, a dependent entry, or a
Provisional since Batch 34: ratified, in force, subject to redesign, saying what it lacked (ADR-0029 A4): ADR-0050, ADR-0052 and four amendments
that depend on them; as at G11 (G12 §1.2).
decisions/README.md gives status at G12 and is a convenience; the checkpoint is the state of record.
theory-of-operation.md, the head: revision 16 (2026.11.16, tag ToO-rev16), cut against G12; revision 15, against G11, stands at G12 and is what
G12's manifest measures. A revision is an edit, a Changes appendix, a commit and a tag.
glossary.md, revised in place and tagged glossary-<date>; 2026.11.16 against G12.
architecture-description.md: a draft, revision 4 against G12, untagged; an arc42 index over the records that decides nothing. G10 measures
revisions/: a closed archive of the dated revisions before the cut (09.10 to rev 9).
One-shot analyses, reviews and assessments. A derived document is never revised; a new one is written. 287 entries in G12's manifest: G11's 32,
twenty-two dated documents and 233 files in five directories (G12 §9); one dated document added after the cut (
topak-sici-assessment-2026.11.16.md). Two directories have no row in derived/README.md (G12 item 12).
Ten accepted records cite files here by path in their provenance notes, so names do not change.
The 09.17 and 09.26 glossaries stay here, frozen, because records cite them.

text.tspan: 3 · How a change moves through the corpus

svg.text: A record is drafted and revised in place while Proposed: History rows
R1, R2 …, each "Applied — Proposed record, revised in place".
The genesis custodian ratifies under ADR-0029 §2, in numbered
batches (G9: Batch 26; G10: Batches 27–35, on two days; G11: 36 and
Accepted (genesis); a confirmation-required marker C1–C4 when the
first post-bootstrap quorum must review it (ADR-0029 §4); provisional
when it did not meet its own ratification condition and says what it
Only typed History rows: an amendment (A1 …), an erratum (E1 …),
or a dependent entry (B22 …) when another record's ratification
A dependent amendment is drafted to be applied as marked, beside
the text it changes (G10 §5); sixteen are pending at G12, fifteen after
Batch 40, all on Proposed records. A pending amendment may be
Gn supersedes Gn−1 as the state of record: ratifications, ledger, open
list. tools/cut-manifest.sh cuts SHA256SUMS-Gn under EXCLUDE;
index.tsv gains a row naming the commit; a tag Gn.
The ToO is edited against the checkpoint, with a "Changes from
revision N" appendix, a commit and a tag ToO-revN; the glossary is
revised in place. Until then the checkpoint wins (G12 item 109 owes rev
mechanism/corpus-pins.sha256: the drift test fails when a pinned
record moves; review, bring the code into line or register the
divergence, then replace the pin line.
An ADR-0033 addendum cites the new SHA256SUMS-REF-<date>.

Example, G10 (2026.10.04–05): ADR-0005 ratified alone in Batch 27 (44ff854) → Batches 28 to 31, among them ADR-0033 A7 ratified ahead of ADR-0036 and the Run profile (9b3cecd, efd83b9) → the reference rebuilt in five stages to records then Proposed, each with an ADR-0033 addendum and a manifest, SHA256SUMS-REF-2026.10.05 to -05e (7764e52, c15026d, c7de2ba, 9c57221, 7d8c7db); A9 accepted alone in Batch 32 → Batch 33, the race (65185ed) → Batch

text.tspan: Two kinds of manifest failure that are correct (counts at

svg.text: SHA256SUMS-G11 fails twelve entries at G12's tree by construction (seven records, the three narrative files, spec/deadlock-audit.sh, spec/proof-certification.md) and verifies 604 of 604 at ce8f460 (G12 §9); thirteen at 1988f93,

SHA256SUMS-REF-2026.11.16 fails two entries at G12's tree, the pin file and the register (§9), and seven at 1988f93, the entries A20 lists; 116 of 116 at d1b72db. -11.16b fails one at 1988f93, the pin file, which moved with Batch 40
(B40); 116 of 116 at 36269bc. SHA256SUMS-G12 fails six at 1988f93: ADR-0033, the three narrative files, spec/modules.tsv and spec/proof-sync.sh; 1,100 of 1,100 at 0a1bc8d.
Frozen records that cite pre-move paths are not edited: their digests are pinned. Two such citations are knowingly left stale and resolve through the layout map.

text.tspan: Pointers still behind the state of record

svg.text: G12's header names revision 15 as the standing narrative; revision 16 is written against G12 afterwards (items 14, 109). The tags item 109 owed, G12 and REF-2026.11.16, and ToO-rev16 and glossary-2026.11.16, are made.
SHA256SUMS-REF-2026.11.16b (A20, B40) has no tag at 2026.11.17, where every earlier reference manifest has one (the diagram's observation).

The floor stages open with a comment that is wrong, "not what the reference follows" (G11 item 91, as at G11 under G12 §7); floor/README.md says the reference links the labels stage, where it links workflow (G12 §2.2), and that
T_persona is not yet read, where it is (ADR-0033 A6); two policy comments call ADR-0049 Proposed (item 98). ADR-0046 §8 still says the cases are "not reported upstream" (G12 item 104).
decisions/README.md gives status at G12 under a column headed "Status at G12". REVIEWERS_GUIDE_README.md, against G12 and revision 16, is kept current outside the manifest (item 99).
